_id: att rung: windupTruthOnly. att010 (joint rigid-body integer/attitude search, nothing deleted) PLUS Wu-1993 carrier phase WIND-UP injected in TRUTH, with the estimator NOT correcting it. One toggle against att010. This measures the raw damage from the largest effect the simulation was knowingly missing.
_delta: errors.phaseWindup.enable: false -> true. Nothing else. estimator.phaseWindup.correct stays false, so truth carries the term and the model does not.
_WHATWINDUPISANDWHYTHEROLESAREINVERTEDHE: For a circularly polarised signal the carrier phase depends on the relative rotation of the transmit and receive antennas ABOUT THE LINE OF SIGHT; one full relative revolution is exactly one cycle. It is pure geometry, no randomness, and the SAME number of cycles on every signal. In classical GNSS it is driven by the satellite's yaw-steering law. In REVERSE GNSS the roles invert: the ground tower TRANSMITS with axes fixed in ECEF and the SPACECRAFT RECEIVES with axes carried by its attitude, so wind-up here is driven by the SPACECRAFT ATTITUDE. That is exactly why it belongs on the att axis and not somewhere else.
_PREREGISTEREDPREDICTIONONE_ATTITUDEDOES: Recorded before the run. Predict the attitude metrics are IDENTICAL to att010 to floating-point noise, and predict it from the code rather than from hope. Wind-up is a function of the tower dipole (common to both rows of an inter-antenna difference), the spacecraft dipole (SpaceAsset.getAntennaPositionsECEF varies the LEVER ARM per antenna and nothing else, so one attitude serves all four phase centres and there is exactly one spacecraft-level boresight_body in the whole config), and the unit line of sight k, which is the only per-antenna quantity. At GEO a 1 m lever arm over a 36000 km range turns k by ~3e-8 rad, so the inter-antenna difference of the wind-up is ~1e-9 cycles. DiffAttitudeBuilder's observable is z_row = phi_i - phi_ref at ONE tower. Wind-up therefore CANCELS AT THE FIRST DIFFERENCE, before the between-tower DD ever runs. tests/test_phase_windup.m asserts this numerically at < 1e-7 cycles rather than leaving it as an argument.
_PREREGISTEREDPREDICTIONTWO_ITISCONSTANT: Predict phaseWindupMaxMinusMin_cycles of order 1e-5 and certainly far below half a cycle. The reasoning: cfg.asset.angularRate_body_radps is [0;0;0], the truth attitude is a CONSTANT Euler computed once by nadirEulerFromEcef, the towers are fixed in ECEF and a GEO is very nearly fixed in ECEF too. Every input to the wind-up is therefore static and the only variation left is the small orbital motion of the satellite within ECEF. A wind-up constant over an arc is absorbed EXACTLY by the float carrier ambiguity, which is constant per (tower, antenna, signal) arc. So predict no movement in position or clock either. THE POINT OF THE RUNG IS THAT THIS IS A MEASURED NUMBER RATHER THAN AN ASSUMPTION: phaseWindupMaxMinusMin_cycles is the quantity that decides it, and phaseWindupEpochsPerLink is the liveness proof that the term was evaluated on every epoch rather than once.
_WHATTHISRUNGCANNOTCLAIM: A null result here is a property of THIS SCENARIO, not of reverse GNSS. Constancy comes from a zero body rate plus a GEO that is nearly stationary in ECEF plus an attitude that is constant in ECEF. A yaw-steering law, a spinning bus, a commanded slew, a drifting or inclined GEO, or a LEO receiver all break it, and wind-up then walks through cycles and is NOT absorbed. Quote this rung as 'wind-up is constant and absorbed in the nadir-locked GEO case, measured', never as 'wind-up does not matter'.
_WHEREWINDUPISLIVEEVENHERE: The UNDIFFERENCED carrier rows, which serve position and clock, do carry it. It does NOT cancel in the ionosphere-free combination: IF is a metres-weighted sum with alpha+beta = 1, which removes a term constant in METRES, and wind-up is constant in CYCLES. W cycles is W*lambda1 metres on L1 and W*lambda2 on L2, so the combination retains W*(alpha*lambda1 + beta*lambda2) = W*c/(f1+f2), the NARROW-LANE wavelength, 106.95 mm or 56 percent of raw L1. The combination that kills it exactly is the wide-lane N1 - N2, and the EKF does not use that row.
_THELIVENESSDISCRIMINATORS: This repo has toggles on record that were ON and inert, so state the tells in advance. (1) The '[PhaseWindup] APPLIED:' line must appear, and phaseWindupNLinks must be 5 towers x 4 antennas x 2 signals = 40 truth-side link-sides. (2) phaseWindupEpochsPerLink must equal the epoch count, NOT 1 -- a 1 would mean the epoch memo froze the accumulator. (3) diffAttMeanNRows must stay 12, matching att010, since nothing in the attitude path is meant to change. (4) If the term is enabled and phaseWindupNLinks comes back 0, ReportRunner raises phaseWindupInert and the unchanged metrics mean nothing.
_THERESULT: MEASURED 3600 s, against att010 RE-RUN ON THIS SAME TREE so the comparison is like-for-like (the re-run reproduced att010's recorded 1.036624 deg exactly, which is what certifies the baseline). LIVENESS FIRST: '[PhaseWindup] APPLIED: 40 link-sides, 3601 epochs each', so the term was evaluated on every epoch of every link and is not an on-but-inert toggle. THE DECISIVE NUMBER: worst per-link max-minus-min over the whole arc is 9.821174e-08 CYCLES -- 1.9e-8 m at L1, seven orders of magnitude below the half cycle that would matter. Wind-up in this scenario is CONSTANT. What is NOT small is the spread of those constants ACROSS links: phaseWindupSpan_cycles 0.04748126, i.e. 9.0 mm at L1 between the most and least wound link, which is exactly the kind of per-link constant a float carrier ambiguity absorbs. METRICS: finalAttitudeError_deg 1.04811841 against att010's 1.03662395 (+1.109 percent), finalAttitudeSigma_deg 1.00944524 against 1.00928671, err/sigma 1.03831 against 1.02709. finalPositionRMS_m 2.119364899 against 2.119316831, a shift of 48 MICROMETRES on a 2.1 m error. meanNIS 92.91161972 against 92.99878877. diffAttMeanNRows 12 in both.
_HOWTHEPREDICTIONSFARED_ONEWRONGONERIGHT: PREDICTION TWO WAS RIGHT AND THEN SOME: predicted a max-minus-min of order 1e-5 cycles, measured 9.82e-08, i.e. two orders MORE constant than predicted. The direction was right and the magnitude was pessimistic. PREDICTION ONE WAS WRONG AS STATED. It said the attitude metrics would be identical to floating-point noise; they are not -- the attitude error moved 1.1 percent, which is small but is a thousand times larger than floating point. The REASONING behind it survives and the measurement confirms it: diffAttResidRMS_m moved from 0.01912696985 to 0.01912655017, a relative change of 2.2e-05, so the DIFFERENCED observable really is untouched, ~500x less affected than the attitude error itself. What the prediction missed is that attitude is not estimated from the differenced rows alone. The UNDIFFERENCED carrier rows carry attitude partials through the lever arm (shouldUseAttitudePartials, carrier), they do see wind-up, and a per-link constant of up to 9 mm perturbs the EKF during the interval in which the float ambiguities are still learning it. The 1.1 percent is that convergence transient, not a failure of the cancellation.
_WHATTHISRUNGSETTLES: The caveat every att rung carried -- that wind-up is unmodelled and therefore every fixed rung is optimistic by an unknown amount -- is now bounded by a measurement instead of an apology. In the nadir-locked GEO case the unknown amount is 1.1 percent of the attitude error and 48 micrometres of position. That is the whole of it. The caveat was not merely overstated on the cancellation argument; it was numerically negligible on the magnitude as well, and the two are separate findings: the differenced observable never sees it (cancellation), and what the undifferenced rows do see is constant to 1e-7 cycles (absorption).
